title: Swap via Pointers
hints: `a` and `b` are local copies of two addresses. `a = b;` re-points *your copy*; the caller's `x` and `y` do not move. To change the caller's ints you have to go through the pointers.
Read and write the pointees with `*a` and `*b`: `int t = *a;` copies x's value out, `*a = *b;` writes y's value into x. And check both pointers for null before any `*`.
